nodes.description: All three reported individuals had cerebral malformations. nodes.description: Reduced histone H4 acetylation at NuA4/TIP60 target loci alters chromatin accessibility and RNA polymerase II-dependent transcription. Bulk RNA sequencing of primary fibroblasts from affected individuals versus controls showed deregulation of multiple genes controlling development, with consistent downregulation of the neurodevelopmental transcription factor LHX9 and the synaptic adhesion molecule KIRREL3, and upregulation of GFPT2, PER1 and HDAC4. PER1 and HDAC4 had previously been mapped as NuA4/TIP60-bound regions, supporting direct rather than incidental dysregulation.

nodes.description: Fibroblasts from affected individuals show upregulated expression of PER1, a core negative-limb component of the transcription-translation feedback loop that generates circadian rhythms, and the authors of the defining report linked this directly to the sleep anomalies seen in all individuals. Independently of the patient data, TIP60 is an established regulator of the mammalian clock: it acetylates the circadian activator BMAL1 during the activating phase of the cycle to recruit BRD4 and P-TEFb and license productive elongation of clock-controlled transcripts. Both observations make circadian transcriptional dysregulation a plausible substrate for the sleep phenotype, but neither establishes it in the human central nervous system.

nodes.description: The facial skeleton and palate derive from cranial neural crest cells. Inactivation of Kat5 in cranial neural crest cells disrupts intermediate metabolism, protein synthesis, proliferation and survival, drastically reducing the neural crest population; heterozygous Kat5 loss in neural crest specifically impairs palatogenesis. The authors of that work concluded that the orofacial clefting seen in individuals with heterozygous KAT5 missense variants is at least partly a cranial-neural-crest defect, which provides the mechanistic bridge from the chromatin lesion to the recognizable facial gestalt and the cleft/high-arched palate.
nodes.id: Impaired Cranial Neural Crest Expansion and Craniofacial Morphogenesis

nodes.description: Purified NuA4/TIP60 complexes containing the patient variants show decreased or abolished ability to acetylate the histone H4 tail in a chromatin context. p.Cys369Ser abolishes activity on both free histones and chromatin; p.Arg53His and p.Ser413Ala are predominantly defective on nucleosomal substrate, consistent with a chromatin-targeting rather than purely catalytic defect. Because complex assembly is preserved, the catalytically dead subunit is expected to occupy complexes that would otherwise contain wild-type KAT5, giving a dominant-interfering effect rather than simple haploinsufficiency.

nodes.description: Severe, early-onset sleep disturbance present in every reported individual and one of the three features named in the disorder. The reported pattern combines sleep-onset delay with repeated night waking, and, in the adult, early sleep offset with increased daytime napping. This is the single most distinctive feature of NEDFASB and the one with a proposed molecular substrate: PER1, a core clock gene and a NuA4/TIP60-bound locus, is upregulated in patient fibroblasts.
